Northwest winds at 10 mph usher drier air and ample afternoon sunshine, aligning model ensembles like the High-Resolution Rapid Refresh (HRRR) with peaks in the low 70s—well below the climatological May normal of 78°F. Observational data from Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (KATL) already shows temperatures rebounding into the upper 60s midday. Realistic challenges include lingering clouds capping heating at 70°F or below, or enhanced insolation pushing into 74°F+ if skies clear fully earlier than forecast; final KATL reading resolves the market late evening.

eventMetadata.context_description: Latest forecast guidance from the China Meteorological Administration (CMA) and global models including ECMWF and GFS ensembles points to a high temperature of around 21°C in Beijing on May 3, driving trader consensus with 42.5% implied probability on that outcome and clustering next-highest odds at 22°C (24.5%) and 20°C (20.3%). Overnight model runs released May 2 refined this outlook, converging on 20-22°C after earlier projections trended warmer; showers possible late May 3 add minor uncertainty. Watch CMA's afternoon update and Beijing observatory data for final positioning ahead of resolution via official airport measurements.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket reflects tight uncertainty in short-range forecasts for Busan's highest temperature on May 3, with Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA) models projecting a maximum near 16°C under persistent rain and 60% precipitation odds from a lingering frontal system, while private sources like Weather.com indicate 18°C and timeanddate.com 16°C. The edge to 18°C (33.5%) over 17°C (31.5%) stems from recent observations of May 2 highs reaching 22-23°C midday before cooling, potential early rain taper allowing brief solar insolation, and light easterly winds limiting cold air advection. Cloud cover remains the key differentiator—full overcast caps peaks at 17°C or below, but partial clearing could lift to 19°C. Updated KMA guidance due later today will refine model ensembles amid below-normal early May averages of ~20°C.
